  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

Too big if any holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across ~5+ files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children once more; third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260512T050823-0b10ff74/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing child IDs, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a success. Do not mix implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260512T050823-0b10ff74/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

`.ddx/executions/20260512T050823-0b10ff74/no_changes_rationale.txt` must contain one:

- `verification_command: <cmd>` — repo cwd; exit 0 closes, nonzero rejects.
- `status: open` + `reason: <retryable>` — open, smart retry.
- `status: proposed` + `reason: <operator needed>` — operator lane.
- `status: blocked` + `reason: <external blocker>` — blocked lane.

No pseudo-statuses. Bare rationales and `status: needs_investigation` reject.

To request orchestrator decomposition, add `orchestrator_action: decompose` alongside `status: open`.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260512T050823-0b10ff74/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260512T050823-0b10ff74/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Mode and overrides

DDX_MODE=bead_execution: edit code/docs for bead AC. Only broad queue-steward default is overridden; tracker, merge-policy, verification, safety stay active. Bead description/AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and project defaults.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-b25eeda8">
    <title>Wire harness model discovery into runner as the source of model authority</title>
    <description>
Replace hardcoded default model selection in `internal/harnesses/codex/runner.go` and `internal/harnesses/claude/runner.go` with cassette-backed `ModelDiscoverySnapshot` selection. Explicit `--model <id>` pins still win.

## Current state

- `internal/harnesses/registry.go` embeds model discovery snapshots for Codex and Claude.
- `internal/harnesses/types.go` defines `ModelDiscoverySnapshot` with `Models []string`, `ReasoningLevels []string`, and `FreshnessWindow`.
- `internal/modelcatalog/tiers.go` from `fizeau-b2c5c826` provides the version-aware ranker: `modelcatalog.Parse(id)` returns `ParsedModel`, and `ParsedModel.Compare(other)` orders same-family models newest and strongest first.
- `internal/modelcatalog/catalog.go` exposes `Catalog.ModelEligibility(id)` and `ModelEntry.AutoRoutable()` for catalog IDs and declared surface IDs.
- The embedded catalog maps Codex model IDs on `modelcatalog.SurfaceCodex` and Claude Code model IDs on `modelcatalog.SurfaceClaudeCode`.

## Problem

Codex and Claude runner defaults are still hardcoded. Adding a newer auto-routable model should require only discovery/catalog evidence, not another runner code edit.

## Scope

1. Add an in-process discovery snapshot cache in `internal/harnesses/discovery_cache.go`, keyed by harness name and snapshot source. For this bead, the source is the embedded cassette snapshot already present in the registry; no live PTY refresh is required.
2. When no operator `--model` pin is provided, each runner loads the cached snapshot, filters `snapshot.Models` through `Catalog.ModelEligibility(modelID)`, keeps only `AutoRoutable == true`, sorts same-family candidates with `modelcatalog.Parse(...).Compare(...)`, and chooses the highest-ranked candidate.
3. Use `modelcatalog.SurfaceCodex` for Codex runner catalog projection and `modelcatalog.SurfaceClaudeCode` for Claude runner catalog projection. The concrete discovery strings `gpt-5.5` and `opus-4.7` are valid catalog surface IDs today.
4. When an explicit `--model <id>` pin is provided, keep using that exact pin. Discovery may warn if the pin is absent from the snapshot, but must not override it.
5. Surface a structured runner/default-resolution signal when the resolved default differs from the prior hardcoded default, so operators can see when discovery changes the selected model.
6. If snapshot lookup fails, fall back to the prior hardcoded default and emit a warning. Do not fail runner construction on discovery errors.

## Non-scope

- ReasoningLevels wiring; that is `fizeau-b0366923`.
- Persistent on-disk discovery storage.
- Live PTY refresh or background goroutine refresh.
- Cross-harness selection or cross-family ranking.

## Expected embedded defaults

Using the current embedded snapshots and catalog:

- Codex no-pin default resolves to `gpt-5.5`.
- Claude no-pin default resolves to `opus-4.7`.
- Codex explicit `--model gpt-5.4` remains `gpt-5.4`.
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. `go test ./internal/harnesses/...` passes with a Codex runner regression proving no `--model` pin plus the embedded Codex snapshot resolves to `gpt-5.5`.
2. `go test ./internal/harnesses/...` passes with a Claude runner regression proving no `--model` pin plus the embedded Claude snapshot resolves to `opus-4.7` via `modelcatalog.SurfaceClaudeCode`.
3. `go test ./internal/harnesses/...` passes with a Codex explicit-pin regression proving `--model gpt-5.4` still resolves to `gpt-5.4`.
4. `go test ./internal/harnesses/...` passes with a discovery-cache regression proving two runner constructions for the same harness and embedded source read the cassette snapshot once.
5. `go vet ./...` passes.
6. No production code in Codex or Claude runners retains the old hardcoded default as the primary no-pin model source; any remaining old default string is only a documented fallback for snapshot lookup failure.
    </acceptance>
    <notes>
Operator resolved intake ambiguity: named the closed ranker API, fixed catalog surfaces, pinned Claude expected default, and removed live-refresh contradiction.
    </notes>
